target_customer: Brazilian infoproducers and online course creators who sell digital products, plus affiliates and buyers on the platform
problem: Creators in Brazil needed payment processing, video hosting and student management in one place at a low cost. Kiwify bundles checkout, video streaming, members area and affiliate management.
business_model: Take rate on each sale (percentage plus fixed fee per transaction), plus receivables advance financing
product_category: Digital product and online course sales platform (creator economy)

founders.name: Artur Ribas
founders.background_notes: Suno reports he and Marinho Gomes worked in digital marketing for almost a decade and met on an online digital marketing forum; company based in Balneario Camboriu.

founders.name: Marinho Gomes
founders.background_notes: Education and employers not found in sources opened.

investors: Itau BBA (lead coordinator of the receivables fund offering)

competitors.name: Hotmart
competitors.what: Largest Latin American infoproduct and affiliate platform; bought Teachable, Klickpages and Wollo in 2020
competitors.traction_then: described as market leader in Latin America

competitors.name: Monetizze
competitors.what: Infoproduct and physical product affiliate platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments, anti-fraud, video streaming and affiliate splits in Brazil involve standard engineering with hard parts around payment compliance and scale.

defensibility.rationale: Producers can move between Hotmart, Eduzz, Monetizze and Kiwify; the differences were price (free video hosting) and features, though buyer and affiliate data add some lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept operating alongside Kiwify. Kiwify grew to more than 30,000 active producers by 2024 per a sponsored Finsiders article; no incumbent acquisition of Kiwify was found.

market_need_then: Online course and infoproduct sales grew during the 2020 pandemic in Brazil according to a Sebrae guide; creators wanted lower fees and bundled video hosting.

branding.domain_note: Uses kiwify.com.br (Brazilian country domain), not an exact .com.

identity.logo: kiwi fruit mark per press descriptions
identity.visual_style: not verified from the site (fetch was rate limited)
identity.voice_and_tone: Informal creator-friendly tone is typical of the category; not verified

branding.community_and_virality: Forbes Brasil ran a brand-supported feature in 2025 and many how-to guides exist. Consumer complaint sites show refund disputes involving the platform. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely compared to Hotmart in how-to guides and Forbes Brasil coverage, which shows recognition in the creator market, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.to: Platform plus receivables financing (FIDC) for producers
pivots.why: Finsiders says Kiwify aims to finance digital businesses through receivables advances

outcome_analysis: Kiwify entered the crowded Brazilian infoproduct market in 2020 against Hotmart, Eduzz and Monetizze, winning producers with free video hosting and low fees. It grew to a team of about 200 and, per a sponsored 2024 article, more than 30,000 active producers and 25 million registered buyers. The documented capital is YC's standard deal plus receivables fund debt of R$50 million in late 2024 and R$150 million in February 2025, not venture equity. Growth appears driven by the product and the creator economy rather than venture funding.
notes: kiwify.com.br could not be fetched (domain safety check rate limited). Debt rounds are in reais (R$50 million late 2024, R$150 million February 2025) and amount_usd is left null because no source gives a dollar figure; Finsiders is a sponsored article, and the 2024 month is stated as end of 2024. CB Insights lists a Series A II of about 25.95M USD on 26 February 2025 with Itau, total about 34.41M over 3 rounds; this is a single aggregator, probably the same FIDC deal, and is not recorded as equity. Competitor source_date is the year reported by the search tool for a comparison of platform fees; the tactus page itself was not opened, so dates are approximate. No source on the name origin was found.
